1.1: Paul a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and our brother Timotheus, unto Philemon our dear friend, and fellow helper,
1.2: And to our dear sister Apphia, and to Archippus our fellow souldier, and to the Church that is in thine house:
1.3: Grace be with you, and peace from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
1.4: I give thanks to my God, making mention alwaies of thee in my praiers,
1.5: (When I hear of thy love and faith, which thou hast toward the Lord Jesus, and toward all Saintes)
1.6: That the fellowship of thy faith may bee made effectuall, and that whatsoever good thing is in you through Christ Jesus, may be knowen.
1.7: For we have great joy and consolation in thy love, because by thee, brother, the Saintes bowels are comforted.
1.8: Wherefore, though I bee very bold in Christ to commaund thee that which is convenient,
1.9: Yet for loves sake I rather beseech thee, though I be as I am, even Paul aged, and even now a prisoner for Jesus Christ.
1.10: I beseech thee for my sonne Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my bondes,
1.11: Which in times past was to thee unprofitable, but now profitable both to thee and to me,
1.12: Whom I have sent again: thou therefore receive him, that is mine own bowels,
1.13: Whom I would have reteined with mee, that in thy stead he might have ministred unto me in the bondes of the Gospel.
1.14: But without thy mind would I doe nothing, that thy benefit should not be as it were of necessitie, but willingly.
1.15: It may be that he therefore departed for a season, that thou shouldest receive him for ever,
1.16: Not now as a servant, but above a servant, even as a brother beloved, specially to me: how much more then unto thee, both in the flesh and in the Lord?
1.17: If therefore thou count our thinges common, receive him as my self.
1.18: If he hath hurt thee, or oweth thee ought, that put on mine accounts.
1.19: I Paul have written this with mine own hand: I will recompense it, albeit I doe not say to thee, that thou owest moreover unto me even thine own self.
1.20: Yea, brother, let mee obteine this pleasure of thee in the Lord: comfort my bowels in the Lord.
1.21: Trusting in thine obedience, I wrote unto thee, knowing that thou wilt do eve more then I say.
1.22: Moreover also prepare mee lodging: for I trust through your prayers I shall be freely given unto you.
1.23: There salute thee Epaphras my felowe prisoner in Christ Jesus,
1.24: Marcus, Aristarchus, Demas and Luke, my felowe helpers.
1.25: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, Amen.  Written from Rome to Philemon, and send by Onesimus a servant.

57:1:6: That by this means all men may perceive how rich you are in Christ, to wit, in faith, charity, and all bountifulness.
By fellowship of faith, he meaneth those duties of charity which are bestowed upon the Saints, and flow forth of an effectual faith.
57:1:7: Because thou didst so dutifully and cheerfully refresh the Saints, that they conceived inwardly a marvelous joy: for by this word (Bowels) is meant not only the inward feeling of wants and miseries that men have one of another’s state, but also that joy and comfort which entereth into the very bowels, as though the heart were refreshed and comforted.
57:1:9: An example of a Christian exercise and commendation for another man.
57:1:12: As mine own son, and as if I had begotten him of mine own body.
57:1:14: That thou mightest not seem to have lent me thy servant upon constraint, but willingly.
57:1:15: Thus he assuageth the harder kind of speech, which is to say, he ran away.
57:1:16: Because he is thy servant, as other servants are, and because he is the Lord’s servant, so that thou must needs love him both for the Lord’s sake, and for thine own sake.
57:1:20: Good brother let me obtain this benefit at thine hand.
